evals.prompt: csvsum/ has no README yet. Write csvsum/README.md for someone who has never seen the tool: what it does, what they need installed, and a quick start they can copy and paste that shows the output they should get.
evals.expected_output: A README with a one-sentence lead, the Python requirement taken from pyproject.toml (3.10 or later), a quick start run from csvsum/ against data/sales.csv whose Expected output block matches the real output (for example 852.75 for the revenue column), all documented commands passing check_doc_commands.py, and no broken links.

assertions.text: Every documented command in README.md runs from csvsum/ and at least one has its expected output shown and matching (check_doc_commands.py).
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_doc_commands.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_doc_commands.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_doc_commands.py"; O=$(python3 "$T" csvsum/README.md --cwd csvsum --timeout 30 2>&1); s=$?; echo "$O"; [ $s -eq 0 ] && echo "$O" | grep -q "^ok " && echo "$O" | grep -q "output matches"

assertions.text: README.md states the Python requirement from pyproject.toml (3.10).
README.md has no broken relative links or anchors (check_links.py).
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_links.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_links.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_links.py"; python3 "$T" csvsum/README.md
